title: AL SB63: Health care plans; to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in determinations of coverage

obligations: A health benefit plan provider that uses artificial intelligence to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall base determinations on the enrollee's medical history, any clinical circumstances unique to the enrollee presented by the requesting health care provider, and additional clinical information about the enrollee in the medical record (Sec. 1(b)(1)).

A health benefit plan provider shall certify annually to the department that the artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization complies with the requirements that it does not rely on a group dataset, is fairly and equitably applied, and does not discriminate directly or indirectly against any subscriber group or enrollee in violation of state or federal law (Sec. 1(b)(2)).

A determination to deny, delay, or modify a request for prior authorization based on medical necessity shall always be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional who is competent to evaluate any recommendation or conclusion of artificial intelligence in light of the specific clinical issues involved in the health care service requested which are unique to the enrollee's circumstances or as recommended by the treating health care provider (Sec. 1(b)(3)).
A health benefit plan provider shall make prominent written disclosure regarding its use of artificial intelligence in utilization review in its policies and procedures (Sec. 1(c)(1)).

A health benefit plan provider shall ensure that its use of artificial intelligence and the outcomes that it generates are reviewed on a periodic basis to maximize accuracy and reliability and to ensure compliance with subsection (b) (Sec. 1(c)(2)).

A health benefit plan provider shall ensure that patient data used in utilization review functions by artificial intelligence is not used beyond its intended and stated purpose consistent with the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), 42 U.S.C. § 1320d et seq. (Sec. 1(c)(3)).

The requirements under subsection (b) and subsection (c) shall be satisfied by an attestation by an authorized representative of the health benefit plan provider based on reasonable reliance upon internal policies, procedures, and third-party vendors (Sec. 1(c)(4)).
When the department notifies a health benefit plan provider of an alleged violation of subsection (b), the health benefit plan provider shall respond to the notice within 30 days (Sec. 1(d)(1)).
prohibitions: Artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall not rely on a group dataset to make determinations (Sec. 1(b)(2)a).

Artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall not discriminate, directly or indirectly, against any subscriber group or enrollee in violation of state or federal law, including any regulation or guidance issued by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (Sec. 1(b)(2)c).
Patient data used in utilization review functions by artificial intelligence shall not be used beyond its intended and stated purpose consistent with HIPAA (Sec. 1(c)(3)).

A determination to deny, delay, or modify a request for prior authorization based on medical necessity shall not be made solely by artificial intelligence; it must be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional (Sec. 1(b)(3)).

What it does

This Alabama law limits how health benefit plan providers may use artificial intelligence to make medical necessity determinations for prior authorization requests. It requires individualized clinical review, annual certification, human clinician final decisions on denials, disclosure, periodic review, and data protections. The Department of Insurance may investigate and discipline violations.

Who it applies to

  • Health benefit plan providers as defined in Sec. 1(a)(6), including entities that issue, deliver, or renew health benefit plans, internal utilization review departments, and separate utilization review contractors or agents
  • The Department of Insurance of the State of Alabama as the enforcing agency

Effective date

October 1, 2026

Key definitions

  • Artificial intelligence: A machine-based system that may include software or physical hardware that performs tasks, based upon data set inputs, which require human-like perception, cognition, planning, learning, communication, or physical action and which is capable of improving performance based upon learned experience without significant human oversight toward influencing real or virtual environments (Sec. 1(a)(1)).
  • Department: The Department of Insurance of the State of Alabama (Sec. 1(a)(2)).
  • Enrollee: An individual to whom a health benefit plan provider is contractually obligated to pay for or provide medical benefits under a health benefit plan (Sec. 1(a)(3)).
  • Group plan: A health benefit plan that is sponsored by an employer or other entity on behalf of group members (Sec. 1(a)(4)).
  • Health benefit plan: Any plan, policy, or contract issued, delivered, or renewed in this state that provides medical benefits that include payment for hospitalization, physician care, treatment, surgery, therapy, drugs, equipment, and any other medical expense, regardless of whether the plan is for a group or individual; the term does not include accident-only, specified disease, individual hospital indemnity, credit, dental-only, Medicare supplement, long-term care, disability income, or other limited benefit health insurance policies, or coverage issued as supplemental to liability insurance, workers' compensation, or automobile medical payment insurance (Sec. 1(a)(5)).
  • Health benefit plan provider: Any entity that issues, delivers, or renews a health benefit plan, including a person as defined in Section 27-1-2, Code of Alabama 1975; a health maintenance organization established under Chapter 21A of Title 27, Code of Alabama 1975; a nonprofit health care services plan established under Article 6, Chapter 20 of Title 10A, Code of Alabama 1975; or a nonprofit agricultural organization that offers health care benefits pursuant to Chapter 33 of Title 2, Code of Alabama 1975; also any department or office internal to such an entity which performs utilization review, and any separate entity that performs utilization review as a contractor or agent of such an entity (Sec. 1(a)(6)).
  • Health care service: Diagnosing, testing, monitoring, or treating a human disease, disorder, syndrome, illness, or injury that may include, but not be limited to, hospitalization, physician care, treatment, surgery, therapy, drugs, or medical equipment (Sec. 1(a)(7)).
  • Individual plan: A health benefit plan that is purchased directly by an individual (Sec. 1(a)(8)).
  • Prior authorization: A written or oral determination made by a health benefit plan provider that a health care service is a benefit covered under the applicable health benefit plan which, under the enrollee's clinical circumstances, is medically necessary or satisfies another requirement imposed by the health benefit plan provider or law and thus satisfies the requirements for payment or reimbursement (Sec. 1(a)(9)).
  • Utilization review: The determination of requests for prior authorization under a health benefit plan according to the rules, health care service policies, and guidelines adopted by a health benefit plan provider, or requirements imposed by law, and applicable to a health benefit plan (Sec. 1(a)(10)).

Obligations

  • A health benefit plan provider that uses artificial intelligence to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall base determinations on the enrollee's medical history, any clinical circumstances unique to the enrollee presented by the requesting health care provider, and additional clinical information about the enrollee in the medical record (Sec. 1(b)(1)).
  • A health benefit plan provider shall certify annually to the department that the artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization complies with the requirements that it does not rely on a group dataset, is fairly and equitably applied, and does not discriminate directly or indirectly against any subscriber group or enrollee in violation of state or federal law (Sec. 1(b)(2)).
  • A determination to deny, delay, or modify a request for prior authorization based on medical necessity shall always be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional who is competent to evaluate any recommendation or conclusion of artificial intelligence in light of the specific clinical issues involved in the health care service requested which are unique to the enrollee's circumstances or as recommended by the treating health care provider (Sec. 1(b)(3)).
  • A health benefit plan provider shall make prominent written disclosure regarding its use of artificial intelligence in utilization review in its policies and procedures (Sec. 1(c)(1)).
  • A health benefit plan provider shall ensure that its use of artificial intelligence and the outcomes that it generates are reviewed on a periodic basis to maximize accuracy and reliability and to ensure compliance with subsection (b) (Sec. 1(c)(2)).
  • A health benefit plan provider shall ensure that patient data used in utilization review functions by artificial intelligence is not used beyond its intended and stated purpose consistent with the federal Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), 42 U.S.C. § 1320d et seq. (Sec. 1(c)(3)).
  • The requirements under subsection (b) and subsection (c) shall be satisfied by an attestation by an authorized representative of the health benefit plan provider based on reasonable reliance upon internal policies, procedures, and third-party vendors (Sec. 1(c)(4)).
  • When the department notifies a health benefit plan provider of an alleged violation of subsection (b), the health benefit plan provider shall respond to the notice within 30 days (Sec. 1(d)(1)).

Prohibitions

  • Artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall not rely on a group dataset to make determinations (Sec. 1(b)(2)a).
  • Artificial intelligence used to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization shall not discriminate, directly or indirectly, against any subscriber group or enrollee in violation of state or federal law, including any regulation or guidance issued by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (Sec. 1(b)(2)c).
  • Patient data used in utilization review functions by artificial intelligence shall not be used beyond its intended and stated purpose consistent with HIPAA (Sec. 1(c)(3)).
  • A determination to deny, delay, or modify a request for prior authorization based on medical necessity shall not be made solely by artificial intelligence; it must be made by a licensed physician or other health care professional (Sec. 1(b)(3)).

Penalties and enforcement

The Department of Insurance of the State of Alabama enforces this section. If the department has reasonable grounds to believe a violation of subsection (b) occurred, it may notify the provider, require a response within 30 days, hold a hearing under Article 1, Chapter 2 of Title 27, Code of Alabama 1975, and impose a corrective plan. For repeat violations indicating a general business pattern or practice, the department may impose an administrative fine of not more than $5,000 and suspend or revoke the certificate of authority. The department shall require the provider to reimburse administrative expenses incurred in investigation and enforcement. The department shall adopt rules to enforce this section. The text does not state a private right of action. (Sec. 1(d)(1)-(4), Sec. 1(e))

How it affects AI deployment

  • A health benefit plan provider deploying AI for prior authorization medical necessity determinations must ensure the AI uses the individual enrollee's medical history, unique clinical circumstances, and additional clinical information, not just group data (Sec. 1(b)(1), Sec. 1(b)(2)a).
  • The provider must annually certify to the Department of Insurance that the AI is fairly and equitably applied and does not discriminate (Sec. 1(b)(2)).
  • Any denial, delay, or modification of prior authorization based on medical necessity must be made by a licensed physician or other competent health care professional, not by AI alone (Sec. 1(b)(3)).
  • The provider must disclose its use of AI in utilization review in policies and procedures, periodically review AI outcomes for accuracy and reliability, and ensure patient data is used only for intended and stated purposes consistent with HIPAA (Sec. 1(c)(1)-(3)).
  • The provider must have an authorized representative attest to compliance based on reasonable reliance on internal policies, procedures, and third-party vendors (Sec. 1(c)(4)).
  • The Department of Insurance may investigate, require corrective plans, impose fines up to $5,000 for repeat violations, suspend or revoke certificates of authority, and require reimbursement of administrative expenses (Sec. 1(d)(1)-(4)).

Notable exemptions

  • The term health benefit plan does not include accident-only, specified disease, individual hospital indemnity, credit, dental-only, Medicare supplement, long-term care, disability income, or other limited benefit health insurance policies, or coverage issued as supplemental to liability insurance, workers' compensation, or automobile medical payment insurance (Sec. 1(a)(5)b).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the organization is a health benefit plan provider that uses artificial intelligence to make determinations of medical necessity on requests for prior authorization under health benefit plans (Sec. 1(a)(6), Sec. 1(b)).
  • Configure AI systems to base determinations on the enrollee's medical history, unique clinical circumstances presented by the requesting provider, and additional clinical information in the medical record (Sec. 1(b)(1)).
  • Ensure AI does not rely on a group dataset, is fairly and equitably applied, and does not discriminate directly or indirectly (Sec. 1(b)(2)).
  • Establish that any denial, delay, or modification of prior authorization based on medical necessity is made by a licensed physician or other competent health care professional (Sec. 1(b)(3)).
  • Make prominent written disclosure of AI use in utilization review in policies and procedures (Sec. 1(c)(1)).
  • Implement periodic review of AI use and outcomes to maximize accuracy and reliability and ensure compliance (Sec. 1(c)(2)).
  • Ensure patient data used in AI utilization review is not used beyond its intended and stated purpose consistent with HIPAA (Sec. 1(c)(3)).
  • Have an authorized representative attest annually to the department based on reasonable reliance on internal policies, procedures, and third-party vendors (Sec. 1(c)(4)).
  • Respond to any department notice of alleged violation within 30 days (Sec. 1(d)(1)).
  • Monitor department rules adopted to enforce this section and adjust practices accordingly (Sec. 1(e)).
